body.statement: As \(\kappa\to\infty\), \(\sqrt\kappa D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\to C_G\) and \(\sqrt\kappa D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\to C_G\). The upper bound is attained by a deterministically calibrated, clipped efficient interval with full-range output on exponentially rare fit failures; the lower bound holds along interior local submodels approaching a maximizer of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
body.justification: The theorem connects exact sparse-count honesty to regular fixed-\(T\) PPML inference and shows that randomization has no first-order high-information advantage.
body.gap: Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004) transfer bounded decision risks between different Poisson and Gaussian experiments; the present bridge profiles the causal nuisance and transfers connected-interval minimax length with target boundaries.
body.consumer: Practitioners obtain a regime check showing when exact certification may be replaced, to first order, by an efficient Gaussian interval.
